post.description:
One allocation by service id. Readable by any authenticated user in any state —
 an investor holding units of a closed product still needs to render it.

The catalog. Any authenticated user sees the `open` allocations; an
 `AllocationManage` holder may set `include_unlisted` to see drafts and closed
 ones too. Ordered by `service`.

Register a new allocation in `draft` (AllocationManage). The service id is a
 1..64 char `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` slug and is immutable once registered; re-registering
 an existing one is a conflict, never a silent update.

Drive the lifecycle (AllocationManage): `open` or `close`. Idempotent — setting
 the state an allocation already holds succeeds and changes nothing.

Resize the authorised unit supply (AllocationManage). Idempotent. Separate from
 UpdateAllocation because this one gates money: `Subscribe` refuses a mint that
 would carry the issued supply past the cap. A cap below what is already issued is
 legal and means "no more units" — nothing minted is affected and redemptions are
 untouched, so this can never strand a holder. Zero is refused: use
 SetAllocationState(`closed`) to stop new money, which says so in the state.

Update the presentation fields of an existing allocation (AllocationManage).
 Never changes state or identity.

Mint the money-plane token pair for an already-identified user, keyed by their
 concierge user id. Service-to-service: authenticated by the shared issuance token
 in the `authorization` metadata (Bearer), never a user token. The user must already
 exist locally (provisioned by the cross-plane bridge) and not be frozen.

Publish the current signing public keys (JWKS). Polled by downstream services'
 `evbanking_auth` verifier to refresh its local cache; also consulted on an
 unknown-`kid` miss. Carries only public key material.

List the caller's active sessions (refresh-token families). Identity is proven by
 the presented refresh token (the BFF holds it server-side); the family that owns
 that token is flagged `current`.

Revoke the presented refresh token's family. With `revoke_all` set, also bumps
 the user's `token_version` so every outstanding access token is rejected hub-side.

Rotate a refresh token: returns a fresh access+refresh pair and invalidates
 the presented refresh token (rotation + reuse detection in the central store).

Revoke one of the caller's sessions by id (must belong to the same user). Revoking
 the current session is allowed (acts like a sign-out of this device).

Cancel a still-QUEUED revenue payout (refund to the revenue claim). Refuses a
 user's withdrawal, and refuses once processing — a broadcast may have landed.

Dispatch a queued withdrawal to custody once its rail has liquidity (the treasury
 worker). Stands in for an automated rebalance/top-up trigger. Idempotent.

Fail a queued fund redemption (operator): voids the reserved burn, returning the
 user's units. Idempotent.

Fail a processing user withdrawal that never reached the chain: voids the
 reservation, refunding the user. NEVER call this if the broadcast may have landed
 on-chain — that would double-pay. Idempotent.

What the fund has EARNED and may pay itself — the `fee` claim, segmented into
 earned / available / pending, plus the rails a payout can ship on. Admin/Owner.
Operator (TreasuryRead): the money-plane operations mode (the read-only kill-switch).

The treasury: per-rail on-chain liquidity (Layer 2) and the claims it backs
 (Layer 1), read live from TigerBeetle (Read-First).
Operator (TreasuryRead): outbox rows the relay parked (needs-intervention).

Operator (RedemptionSettle): the cross-user queue of redemptions awaiting settle,
 oldest first — the "Valuation & redemptions" screen's clear-the-queue surface.
 (Est. cash = units × current NAV is computed client-side from the posted NAV.)
The fund's own payouts, newest first — the payout history. Admin/Owner.

Admin (WithdrawalSettle): the cross-user queue of withdrawals awaiting operator
 action, oldest first — `queued` (awaiting liquidity/dispatch) and `processing`
 (broadcast in flight: settle with the mined tx ref, or fail ONLY if nothing
 reached the chain). The admin Withdrawals screen's clear-the-queue surface.

Post a fund's total AUM; NAV is derived = AUM / units_outstanding (units read live
 from TigerBeetle). Rejects zero units and, unless `override` is set, a NAV move
 beyond the safety threshold vs the last mark (the fat-finger guard on the trust seam).

Record a settled on-chain deposit, crediting a party's claim. Idempotent by
 `tx_ref` — recording the same chain tx twice credits once.

Pay the fund's own earned revenue out to an external wallet (Admin/Owner). Capped
 by `FundRevenue.available`: client claims and the fund's seed capital are different
 ledger accounts and are unreachable from here. Runs the same saga as a user
 withdrawal — accepted and queued when the rail is short, then dispatched/settled
 through the usual operator RPCs — so it shares the withdrawal queue and history.

Admin (DepositAddressRotate): supersede a user's PROVABLY DEAD deposit address
 (the signer can no longer unseal its key — the KEK-epoch casualty class) with a
 freshly minted keypair, and refresh the hub's address cache. The signer refuses
 to rotate a key that still unseals. Funds already on the old address remain
 unrecoverable; this restores the user's ability to receive FUTURE deposits.
Inject the company's own capital onto a rail (Dr WALLET / Cr FUND).

Admin (OperationsManage): toggle read-only mode. When on, every user money mutation
 (withdraw / subscribe / redeem) is rejected — "pause deposits & withdrawals".

Settle a queued fund redemption once the fund's claim is liquid (the treasury
 worker): prices at the settle-time NAV and pays the cash. Idempotent.

Settle a user withdrawal once it has the required on-chain confirmations: posts the
 reservation and moves the net out of custody. `tx_ref` is the chain transaction.
 Stands in for a chain watcher + custody confirmation callback. Idempotent.

Admin (OutboxManage): clear `parked_at` so the relay re-drives the event once the
 cause is fixed; refused for a compensated row — it parked half-applied with
 compensation owed, so re-driving would re-apply the legs that already posted.

The redacted invitation behind an emailed token. Side-effect free. Unknown,
 expired, spent and wrong-state tokens all return the SAME NOT_FOUND, so this
 cannot be used to probe which is which.

Cast this owner's vote. Requires the token AND the secret code from the mail.
 Five failed code attempts burn the token permanently.
Withdraw an invoice the caller opened, while it is still OPEN.
One consilium in full, including per-voter state (Owner only).
Consilia newest first — the governance history (Owner only).

Open an invoice to pay fund revenue out on-chain (Owner only). Refused when a
 consilium is already open — one at a time removes the concurrent-approval
 overdraw race instead of trying to win it — or when the roster is too small.

What the caller's holding owes right now WITHOUT charging it: the management fee
 accrued since the last charge, the performance fee that would crystallize at
 today's NAV, and any carried debt. This is what a position's "value net of fees"
 must subtract, and it carries the investor's own mark so the figure is explicable.

One fund's terms, or an empty policy when the product charges nothing. Readable
 by any authenticated user — an investor is entitled to know what they are paying.

The fund's accumulated, unconverted fee units and what they are worth
 (AllocationManage).

The caller's own fee statement, newest first — every charge, what it was for, and
 anything that deferred.
Every configured policy, ordered by service. Readable by any authenticated user.
Every charge against one fund (AllocationManage).

Install or replace a fund's terms (AllocationManage — the same trust seam as
 bringing the product into existence or posting its valuation). The service must
 already be a registered allocation. Rates are basis points and each is capped at
 10000; a rate above 100% of the thing it is charged on is always a fat finger.

Convert accumulated fee units into fee revenue (AllocationManage). Omit `units`
 to settle the whole balance. Refused — never queued — when the fund's claim
 cannot cover the payout: nobody is waiting on this, and unconverted fee units
 keep accumulating at no cost.
Cancel a still-queued redemption (returns the reserved units).
The current NAV (price per share) for a fund, plus freshness.
The caller's position in one fund (units, NAV, value, cost basis, P&L).
All of the caller's fund positions.
The caller's redemptions for the fund surface (newest first).
Redeem `units` of a fund back to cash (accept-and-queue; settle-time priced).

Subscribe `amount` of free balance into a fund, minting units at the current NAV.
 Returns the mint receipt; the holding updates once the relay applies it.
The caller's operations, newest first, across all four kinds.

Admin (allowlist): disable a user, freezing future sign-in/refresh without
 deleting the record.

The calling user's live balance, read straight from TigerBeetle (Read-First).
 No Postgres-stored amount exists; the response is authoritative as of `as_of`.
The calling user's own identity (resolved from the access-token `sub`).

Admin (UserBalanceRead): read ANY user's live balance by id — the operator
 console's user-detail drawer. The self-service GetBalance above acts on the
 caller's own `sub`; this one takes an explicit target and is role-gated.

Admin (allowlist): bump a user's token_version so all their outstanding access
 tokens are rejected hub-side. The token-revocation control surface.

Update the caller's own editable profile fields (full-replace of the set in
 UpdateProfileRequest). Identity/auth fields (email, status) are not editable here.

Cancel one of the caller's still-queued withdrawals (refund). Rejected once the
 withdrawal is processing (a broadcast may have landed).
The caller's deposit address on a network (stable; derived once and reused).

The caller's wallet — the unified lifecycle balance, deposit addresses, and the
 per-rail withdrawable view.
The caller's confirmed on-chain deposits, newest first.
The caller's withdrawals, newest first.

Request an on-chain withdrawal of free balance to an external address. Accepted
 (and reserved) as long as the unified balance covers it; it ships immediately when
 the chosen rail is liquid, otherwise it is queued until the treasury tops it up.

Exchange a Google authorization code (with its PKCE verifier) for concierge's
 OWN tokens. Called by the cabinet BFF on the OAuth callback. Provisions the
 user on first sign-in in the directory module.

Publish the current signing public keys (JWKS). Polled by downstream services'
 `evconcierge_auth` verifier to refresh its local cache; also consulted on an
 unknown-`kid` miss. Carries only public key material.

List the caller's active sessions (refresh-token families). Identity is proven by
 the presented refresh token (the BFF holds it server-side); the family that owns
 that token is flagged `current`.

Revoke the presented refresh token's family. With `revoke_all` set, also bumps
 the user's `token_version` so every outstanding access token is rejected.

Rotate a refresh token: returns a fresh access+refresh pair and invalidates
 the presented refresh token (rotation + reuse detection in the central store).

Revoke one of the caller's sessions by id (must belong to the same user). Revoking
 the current session is allowed (acts like a sign-out of this device).
Withdraw an admission the caller opened, while it is still OPEN.
Withdraw a proposal the caller opened, while it is still OPEN.
The current owner roster (Owner only).

post.summary:
Propose GRANTING a seat (Owner only). The candidate does not vote — they are not
 yet an owner — and neither does the initiator, so the voters are every OTHER
 current owner and all of them must agree. A lone owner cannot open one at all.
post.description:
This is the only way `Role::Owner` is granted: UserDirectory.SetRole refuses it
 outside an executed admission.

Propose removing an owner (Owner only). The initiator casts no vote — proposing is
 not agreeing, and counting it would let two owners remove a third.

Resign your own seat. No consilium — but the same floor applies, so the last two
 owners cannot leave the fund without governance.

A peer owner's vote on an admission, cast in the cabinet while signed in. One
 REJECT ends it: admission passes only on unanimity.

A peer owner's vote, cast in the cabinet while signed in — this is the live
 consilium, not an emailed link. The target and the initiator are both refused.

Enqueue one governance mail. Idempotent by `dedupe_key`, so an at-least-once
 caller may retry without sending twice.

The redacted invitation behind an emailed token. Unknown, expired, spent and
 wrong-state tokens all return the same NOT_FOUND.

The target accepting — or refusing — their own removal. Five failed code attempts
 burn the token permanently.

Admin (allowlist): disable a user, freezing future sign-in/refresh without
 deleting the record. Emits SUSPENDED across the cross-plane bridge.
The calling user's own identity (resolved from the access-token `sub`).

Admin (UserRead): the full profile of ANY user by id (the admin sibling of the
 self-only GetMe), for the user-detail drawer.

Admin (UserRead): list/search users for the operator console — paginated, with a
 free-text query and optional role/status filters (see ListUsersRequest). Returns
 lightweight summaries, not full profiles.

Admin (allowlist): re-enable a disabled user, lifting the sign-in/refresh
 freeze. Emits REINSTATED across the cross-plane bridge.

Admin (allowlist): bump a user's token_version so all their outstanding access
 tokens are rejected. The token-revocation control surface.

Admin (allowlist): set a user's KYC level. Emits KYC_CHANGED across the
 cross-plane bridge (so the money plane learns the new level). Echoes the
 level now in effect.

Admin (RoleGrant, Owner only): set a user's platform access role. Emits
 ROLE_CHANGED across the cross-plane bridge so the money plane mirrors it. Echoes
 the role now in effect.

Update the caller's own editable profile fields (full-replace of the set in
 UpdateProfileRequest). Identity/auth fields (email, status) are not editable here.

performance.title: performance
performance.description: what would crystallize at today's NAV

high_water_mark.title: high_water_mark
high_water_mark.description: the investor's own mark — why their fee differs

banking.v1.AccruedFees.title: AccruedFees
banking.v1.AccruedFees.description: What a holding owes right now. `configured` is false when the fund charges no fee.

user_id.title: user_id
user_id.description:
The target: the CONCIERGE user id (the handle the operator console carries from
 the identity plane's ListUsers) or the banking user id. Resolution is
 concierge-first via the bridge mirror (`users.concierge_user_id`), falling back
 to the banking id (existing money-plane callers stay valid); an id matching
 neither returns NOT_FOUND — never an authoritative zero.

service.title: service
service.description: the slug — the id used by every FundsService RPC

summary.title: summary
summary.description: one-line description for the catalog card

banking.v1.Allocation.title: Allocation
banking.v1.Allocation.description:
One registered investable product. Carries no money: units, NAV and positions are
 read from FundsService against the same `service` id.

banking.v1.Balance.title: Balance
banking.v1.Balance.description:
The user's single, network-agnostic balance, segmented by lifecycle. Every figure is
 a TigerBeetle-authoritative decimal USDT string; total = available + invested +
 pending_withdrawal.

payload_hash.title: payload_hash
payload_hash.description:
Hex SHA-256 over the canonical terms. Shown (short prefix) in the mail so an owner
 can tell that what they approved is what will execute.

owner_count.title: owner_count
owner_count.description: N — owners at open. The threshold is frozen from this, never recomputed later.

approvals.title: approvals
approvals.description: Votes that are still valid: an approver who has since lost ownership does not count.

version.title: version
version.description:
Monotonic per consilium. The live page watches this and refetches when it moves —
 the socket carries a version, never a tally.

voter_email.title: voter_email
voter_email.description:
The recipient's own masked address, so they can confirm the mail reached the right
 seat before typing the code.

decision.title: decision
decision.description: This seat's own answer, so a reopened link shows what was already said.

attempts_remaining.title: attempts_remaining
attempts_remaining.description: Code attempts left before the token burns.

banking.v1.ConsiliumInvitation.title: ConsiliumInvitation
banking.v1.ConsiliumInvitation.description:
What the emailed owner is shown BEFORE they vote. Deliberately narrower than
 `Consilium`: no other owner's identity, no vote-by-vote breakdown.

banking.v1.ConsiliumState.title: ConsiliumState
banking.v1.ConsiliumState.description: Where a consilium stands. Terminal everywhere except OPEN.

email.title: email
email.description: Masked (`a***@example.com`) on every surface a non-owner can reach.

notified.title: notified
notified.description: True once the mail has actually been handed to the delivery queue.

banking.v1.ConsiliumVoter.title: ConsiliumVoter
banking.v1.ConsiliumVoter.description: One owner's seat in a consilium.

created_at.title: created_at
created_at.description: unix seconds the hub recorded the credit

banking.v1.Deposit.title: Deposit
banking.v1.Deposit.description: A confirmed on-chain deposit credited to the caller's unified balance.

min_confirmations.title: min_confirmations
min_confirmations.description: confirmations before a deposit is credited

is_testnet.title: is_testnet
is_testnet.description:
Whether this rail is on testnet — the client uses it to render the correct address
 form (e.g. TON's testnet-tagged user-friendly address). Only meaningful per rail; false
 for a mainnet rail.

banking.v1.DepositScanCursor.title: DepositScanCursor
banking.v1.DepositScanCursor.description:
Seconds since a rail's deposit watcher last advanced/touched its per-network scan
 cursor (refreshed only by a completed scan cycle, so age ≈ time since the last
 healthy cycle; thresholds are the consumer's concern).

nav.title: nav
nav.description: the price the charge was measured and taken at

debt_opening.title: debt_opening
debt_opening.description: uncollected fee carried INTO this charge

debt_carried.title: debt_carried
debt_carried.description: what deferred to the next charge

high_water_mark.title: high_water_mark
high_water_mark.description: the investor's mark AFTER this charge

banking.v1.FeeAssessment.title: FeeAssessment
banking.v1.FeeAssessment.description:
One charge against one holding. `due` and `charged_cash` differ exactly when the
 holding could not cover the charge and the rest deferred into `debt_carried`.

performance_bps.title: performance_bps
performance_bps.description: 2000 = 20% of the gain above the mark

hurdle_bps.title: hurdle_bps
hurdle_bps.description: 0 = no hurdle; else the p.a. rate the gain must clear first

basis.title: basis
basis.description:
invested_capital | market_value — what the management fee is charged on.
 `invested_capital` (the default) is the cash the investor actually put in: it does
 not swell with a mark the operator posted, which keeps the fee the operator earns
 independent of the input the operator supplies.

crystallization.title: crystallization
crystallization.description:
monthly | quarterly | semi_annual | annual — how often the performance fee
 crystallizes and the mark ratchets. This is a price, not a detail: crystallizing
 more often measurably raises what an investor pays over a fund's life, because
 each reset locks in gains a later loss can no longer claw back.

banking.v1.FeePolicy.title: FeePolicy
banking.v1.FeePolicy.description:
One fund's fee terms. `configured` is false when the product has no policy at all,
 which is different from a policy whose rates happen to be zero.

banking.v1.FeeShares.title: FeeShares
banking.v1.FeeShares.description: The manager's uncollected fee units in one fund.

aum.title: aum
aum.description: last posted AUM (decimal USDT; empty if seed)

units_outstanding.title: units_outstanding
units_outstanding.description: decimal units in circulation (the NAV denominator)

posted_at.title: posted_at
posted_at.description: unix seconds of the mark (0 = seed)

unit_cap.title: unit_cap
unit_cap.description:
The allocation's authorised unit supply and what is left of it. `remaining_capacity`
 counts in-flight mints as issued, so a client that offers it can never offer more
 than Subscribe will accept. decimal units

remaining_capacity.title: remaining_capacity
remaining_capacity.description: decimal units still issuable (0 once at the cap)

banking.v1.FundNav.title: FundNav
banking.v1.FundNav.description:
The current price of a fund's share, derived (AUM / units_outstanding) and frozen
 between operator marks. `posted_at` is 0 when the fund has never been marked (seed
 NAV 1.0); `stale` is true when the latest mark is older than the dealing window.

banking.v1.FundRevenue.title: FundRevenue
banking.v1.FundRevenue.description:
The fund's OWN money — what it earned, not what it custodies. `earned` is the `fee`
 claim, credited by exactly two things: the fee retained on a user withdrawal, and the
 settled management + performance fee (the "2 and 20").
 `earned = available + pending_payout` by construction (all three are read off one
 ledger balance), so the figures can never disagree about a payout in flight.

token.title: token
token.description: The opaque single-use token from the mail. Never the code.

concierge_user_id.title: concierge_user_id
concierge_user_id.description:
The concierge canonical user id (a UUID) of the already-authenticated user. Banking
 maps it to its local mirror row (provisioned by the cross-plane bridge) and mints the
 money-plane pair for that user. Banking never sees Google's `sub` — the bridge carries
 it; the BFF carries this concierge id, which it has from the concierge sign-in.

user_agent.title: user_agent
user_agent.description:
Device metadata captured by the BFF at sign-in, stored on the refresh-token family
 for the "sessions & devices" surface. Best-effort, free-form.

banking.v1.Jwk.title: Jwk
banking.v1.Jwk.description:
One JSON Web Key. Ed25519 keys are OKP: kty="OKP", crv="Ed25519", x=base64url
 public key, alg="EdDSA". `kid` is a stable thumbprint of the public key.

include_unlisted.title: include_unlisted
include_unlisted.description:
Include `draft` and `closed` allocations. Requires AllocationManage; a caller
 without it is refused rather than silently downgraded to the open-only list.

limit.title: limit
limit.description: Rows to return. 0 means the server default (100); the server caps it at 200.

refresh_token.title: refresh_token
refresh_token.description: The caller's current refresh token: proves identity and flags the current session.

revoke_all.title: revoke_all
revoke_all.description:
When true, bump the user's token_version (coarse "revoke all"), not just this
 refresh family.

withdrawable.title: withdrawable
withdrawable.description: max requestable on this rail (= available)

withdrawal_fee.title: withdrawal_fee
withdrawal_fee.description: flat network fee retained on a withdrawal

banking.v1.NetworkWithdrawable.title: NetworkWithdrawable
banking.v1.NetworkWithdrawable.description:
Per-rail withdrawal options (the accept-and-queue UX). `withdrawable` is the whole
 available balance (a request beyond `instant` is accepted and queued); `instant` is
 the portion that ships without queueing = min(available, rail liquidity).

id.title: id
id.description:
Unique within the feed: the aggregate UUID for a withdrawal / subscription /
 redemption, the on-chain `tx_ref` for a deposit (which has no surrogate id).

state.title: state
state.description:
Lifecycle, per kind. deposit: always `credited` (the row exists only once the
 watcher has confirmed it). subscription: always `completed` (an immutable mint).
 withdrawal: queued | processing | completed | failed | cancelled.
 redemption: queued | completed | failed | cancelled.
 fee: `charged` when the whole charge was collected, `partly_deferred` when the
 holding could not cover it and the rest was carried as debt to the next charge.

created_at.title: created_at
created_at.description: unix seconds the hub recorded the operation

amount.title: amount
amount.description:
Cash moved, as a magnitude — the sign is implied by `kind`, never encoded here.
 Empty for a redemption that has not settled yet (settle-time pricing).

net_amount.title: net_amount
net_amount.description: withdrawal only — amount − fee, what ships on-chain

units.title: units
units.description: fund kinds — units minted (subscription) or burned (redemption)

nav.title: nav
nav.description: fund kinds — price dealt at (empty until a redemption settles)

network.title: network
network.description: rail kinds — bep20 | polygon | trc20 | ton

tx_ref.title: tx_ref
tx_ref.description: rail kinds — the on-chain reference (empty until settled)

management.title: management
management.description:
fee only — the two legs of the charge, so the row can say WHY it was taken rather
 than only how much. `management` is rent on parked capital and is charged whether
 the fund gained or not; `performance` is the share of the gain above this
 investor's own high-water mark, and is zero except at a crystallization.

banking.v1.Operation.title: Operation
banking.v1.Operation.description:
One row of the timeline. `kind` is the discriminator — it decides which of the
 remaining fields carry a value; the rest are empty. Deliberately flat rather than a
 oneof: the whole surface is projected to TypeScript through OpenAPI, where a flat
 message with a documented discriminator survives the pipeline unambiguously.

 | field        | deposit | withdrawal | subscription | redemption | fee        |
 | ------------ | ------- | ---------- | ------------ | ---------- | ---------- |
 | amount       | ✓       | ✓ (gross)  | ✓ (cash in)  | ✓ at settle| ✓ (taken)  |
 | fee          |         | ✓          |              |            |            |
 | net_amount   |         | ✓          |              |            |            |
 | units / nav  |         |            | ✓            | ✓ at settle| ✓          |
 | service      |         |            | ✓            | ✓          | ✓          |
 | network      | ✓       | ✓          |              |            |            |
 | address      |         | ✓          |              |            |            |
 | tx_ref       | ✓       | ✓ at settle|              |            |            |
 | management   |         |            |              |            | ✓          |
 | performance  |         |            |              |            | ✓          |

 The `fee` row is the one the investor did not initiate: the fund charging its own
 management and performance fee against the holding. It moves no cash and touches no
 chain — units are clawed back to the manager on the share ledger — so `amount` is what
 those units were WORTH at `nav`, not a transfer. Without this row an investor's units
 would simply shrink with nothing on the timeline to explain it.

truncated.title: truncated
truncated.description:
True when the caller's history is longer than `limit` — the client is looking at
 the newest page, not the whole record.

banking.v1.ParkedEvent.title: ParkedEvent
banking.v1.ParkedEvent.description:
One parked outbox row. `reason` is the relay's last error; `parked_at` is unix
 seconds; `compensated` marks a half-applied event that is owed compensation
 (never unparkable).

cost_basis.title: cost_basis
cost_basis.description: net cash invested, average cost (decimal USDT)

nav_as_of.title: nav_as_of
nav_as_of.description: unix seconds of the NAV mark (0 = seed NAV)

banking.v1.Position.title: Position
banking.v1.Position.description:
A user's holding in one fund. `value = units × nav`; `pnl = value − cost_basis`
 (a signed decimal — losses are negative). `nav_as_of` is the unix-seconds timestamp
 of the NAV mark used (0 when the fund is on the bootstrap seed NAV).

aum.title: aum
aum.description: decimal USDT — the fund's total assets under management

override.title: override
override.description: bypass the NAV-move safety guard (operator confirmed)

custody.title: custody
custody.description: liquid on-chain USDT held in this rail's custody wallet

treasury_address.title: treasury_address
treasury_address.description: the rail's hot wallet — fund USDT (liquidity) + gas here

onchain_usdt.title: onchain_usdt
onchain_usdt.description: decimal USDT actually on-chain in the treasury wallet

onchain_gas.title: onchain_gas
onchain_gas.description: decimal native units (BNB | TRX | TON) for gas

gas_station_address.title: gas_station_address
gas_station_address.description:
The rail's sweep GAS-STATION wallet — a separate account paying the gas drops
 that consolidate user deposits into the treasury. Fund the native coin here,
 never USDT. Empty when the rail has no gas-station view.

is_testnet.title: is_testnet
is_testnet.description:
Whether the addresses above are testnet-tagged, so a client can render them in the
 rail's user-facing form (e.g. TON's testnet-tagged friendly address). Only
 meaningful per rail; false where the rail's address form is network-agnostic.

banking.v1.RailLiquidity.title: RailLiquidity
banking.v1.RailLiquidity.description:
Per-rail on-chain liquidity (the treasury / Layer 2). The `treasury_*`/`onchain_*`
 fields are the operator funding view, read best-effort from the chain — empty means
 the rail is unconfigured or the read was unavailable, never an error.

scan_cursors.title: scan_cursors
scan_cursors.description:
Per-rail deposit-scan diagnostics; only configured rails appear. A large age on
 a configured rail means the deposit scan is stalled — deposits confirm on-chain
 but are not credited. Diagnostics only: it does NOT gate `ready`.

unseal_failures.title: unseal_failures
unseal_failures.description:
Signer unseal failures seen on money-moving paths (sweep / withdrawal signing)
 since this instance booted. Any non-zero value means a PROVABLY DEAD key (the
 KEK-epoch bug class) was asked to sign — funds on its address cannot move.
 Diagnostics only: it does NOT gate `ready`.

banking.v1.ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse
banking.v1.ReadinessResponse.description:

 not-ready response says *why* without scraping logs. `parked_rows` are outbox
 events the relay could not apply (need operator intervention); `backlog` is the
 count of undispatched rows and the age of the oldest, surfacing a wedged relay.

banking.v1.RecordDepositRequest.description:

 therefore cannot mint a balance by typing one — the worst a wrong reference can do is
 name a transfer that does not exist, or one that did not land on an address of ours,
 and both are rejected.

tags.name: banking.v1.AllocationsService
tags.description:
AllocationsService — the registry of investable products (the Allocation primitive).

 An allocation is the control-plane record that makes a service id investable. It is
 the ONLY way one comes into existence: `FundsService.Subscribe` refuses a service
 with no registered, open allocation, so a user can never mint a fund by typing an
 unknown slug. Money never flows through this service — amounts, units and NAV stay
 on FundsService/BalanceService; here live identity, presentation and lifecycle only.

 Lifecycle: `draft` (registered, not yet accepting money) → `open` (subscribe +
 redeem) → `closed` (redeem only, so a closed product never traps an investor).
 `closed` → `open` re-opens. Registration and every transition require
 `AllocationManage` (Admin/Owner) — the same trust seam as posting a valuation.

 Reads are open to any authenticated user; `ListAllocations` returns only `open`
 allocations unless the caller holds `AllocationManage` and asks for all. See
 docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

tags.name: banking.v1.AuthService
tags.description:
AuthService — the money plane's token issuance and authorization surface.

 This is the MONEY plane: it does NOT do third-party (Google) OAuth — identity and
 sign-in live wholly in the concierge plane. Users are mirrored here by the one-way
 cross-plane bridge (concierge `CREATED` → a local row keyed by `auth_subject`).
 This service only issues/rotates the hub's OWN first-party asymmetric JWTs
 (EdDSA/Ed25519, `aud=banking-core`) for those already-identified users, and
 publishes verification keys. Services do NOT call this per request to authorize:
 they verify access tokens locally against the cached JWKS via the shared
 `evbanking_auth` flow (no round trip, no per-service token storage). They DO call
 `Jwks` periodically to refresh that cache, since the hub speaks only gRPC (no HTTP
 `.well-known` endpoint).

 `IssueUserToken` is the concierge→banking token-exchange seam: after the cabinet
 BFF authenticates a user against concierge, it calls this server-to-server (with the
 shared bridge issuance token, NOT a user token) to mint the money-plane pair for that
 user. Banking trusts its OWN service credential, never concierge's issuer — so a
 leaked concierge token can't move money. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

tags.name: banking.v1.FundsService
tags.description:
FundsService — a user's investment in funds via the service currency (units/shares).

 Subscribing buys units at the current NAV; a holding's value is units × NAV, so
 profit comes from NAV rising, not from extra units. Redeeming is accept-and-queue:
 units are reserved immediately and the cash is priced + paid at settle (settle-time
 NAV). Every amount/unit/price is a decimal STRING (proto3 has no u128; a string is
 lossless and matches proto-loader's `longs: String`). Self-service RPCs act on the
 caller's own access-token `sub`. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

tags.name: banking.v1.WalletService
tags.description:
WalletService — a user's own crypto wallet: one unified USDT balance, deposit
 addresses, and withdrawals. Networks (BEP20/Polygon/TRC20/TON) are a transaction attribute
 (where you deposit / where a withdrawal ships), never a balance dimension — the user
 holds a single fungible USDT balance, segmented by lifecycle.

 Every RPC acts on the caller's own access-token `sub`. Balances are read live from the
 authoritative TigerBeetle ledger (Read-First); amounts are decimal USDT STRINGS
 (proto3 has no u128; a string is lossless and matches proto-loader's `longs: String`).
 A withdrawal is a queued saga (reserve → dispatch → settle/void): it is accepted even
 when the chosen rail is short on liquidity and queued until the treasury tops it up.
 The operator-driven dispatch/settle/fail RPCs live on BalanceService; the custody
 broadcast and deposit-address derivation sit behind ports (a stub in this scaffold).
 See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and piggybank/core/PATTERNS.md.

tags.name: banking.v1.BalanceService
tags.description:
BalanceService — the bank's treasury and company capital (operator surface).

 Reads authoritative balances from the TigerBeetle ledger; metadata and events from
 Postgres. Every amount is a decimal USDT STRING (proto3 has no u128; a string is
 lossless and matches proto-loader's `longs: String`). All RPCs are admin-gated
 (allowlist) at the boundary. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

tags.name: banking.v1.ConsiliumService
tags.description:
ConsiliumService — multi-owner authorization for the fund paying its OWN earned
 revenue out. One owner opens an invoice; strictly more than half of ALL owners must
 each confirm it from their mailbox before a single cent moves.

 WHY THE MONEY PLANE OWNS THIS. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md rejects letting a
 concierge-signed artifact authorize money movement, and a consilium verdict is
 exactly such an artifact. So the tally is computed, stored and verified here, against
 the owner roster this plane already mirrors (`0016_user_role.sql`). Concierge is used
 only to DELIVER the mail, over a typed payload it renders itself.

 QUORUM. `threshold = floor(N / 2) + 1` where N is the owner count at open. The
 initiator is in the denominator but gets NO vote and is never minted a token — so
 opening a request can never lower the bar the initiator has to clear. N < 3 makes
 the threshold unreachable and is refused at open rather than parked forever.

 IMMUTABILITY. There is no edit RPC. `payload_hash` binds every approval to the exact
 terms shown in the mail; changing anything means cancel and reopen, and votes are not
 carried over. See docs/CONSILIUM.md for the full policy and threat model.

tags.name: banking.v1.ConsiliumApprovalService
tags.description:
ConsiliumApprovalService — the surface an emailed owner reaches. Mounted OUTSIDE the
 user-auth layer, exactly as AuthService is: the emailed token IS the credential, and
 the owner clicking it may not be signed in.

 The GET is strictly read-only because mail scanners (Gmail, Outlook SafeLinks,
 corporate gateways) issue automatic requests for every URL in a message. The vote is
 a separate call carrying the secret code from the same mail — that is what turns a
 scanned link into a deliberate human act.

tags.name: banking.v1.FeesService
tags.description:
FeesService — a fund's management and performance fee ("2 and 20").

 Two charges, answering different questions. **Management** (2% p.a. by default) is
 rent on parked capital: it accrues continuously with elapsed time and is charged
 whether the fund made money or not. **Performance** (20% by default) is a share of
 profit above the investor's OWN high-water mark, crystallized at the end of a
 period. A product with no policy charges nothing — the fee is opt-in per product.

 The mark is PER INVESTOR, not per fund. That is what stops one investor from paying
 for another's timing: somebody who subscribed at the top pays only on gains above
 the price they actually paid, and somebody who subscribed after a drawdown does not
 ride the recovery fee-free. (A fund-level mark, which a tokenized vault is forced
 into, mutualizes both.)

 A fee is collected by clawing back UNITS — the holder's fund units move to the
 manager's fee-unit account on the share ledger — never by moving cash. So: no chain
 fee is ever paid to collect a fee, an investor's cash balance is untouched and
 cannot be driven negative, and because total units outstanding do not change, NAV
 per unit does not move and no other investor pays for the charge. What cannot be
 collected (units locked by a queued redemption, or a residue below one base unit)
 is carried as debt and taken next time; it is never written off.

 SettleFeeShares is the one operation that crosses into cash, converting a whole
 fund's accumulated fee units in one go rather than once per investor. Amounts and
 prices are exact decimal strings. See piggybank/core/PATTERNS.md and docs/FEES.md.

tags.name: banking.v1.HealthService
tags.description:
Health surface for the hub's gRPC service plane.

   Check     — liveness: is the process up? Trivial, unauthenticated; backs the
               `cabinet` BFF smoke path (browser -> BFF -> gRPC) and service checks.
   Readiness — can this instance actually move money? Pings Postgres + TigerBeetle
               and inspects the outbox (parked rows / dispatch backlog). An
               orchestrator/LB drains an instance that is up but not ready instead of
               routing money-moving traffic to it.

tags.name: banking.v1.OperationsService
tags.description:
OperationsService — the caller's activity timeline: every money event that touched
 their account, in one time-ordered stream.

 A pure CQRS **read model**. The four things a user does — deposit, withdraw,
 subscribe, redeem — are separate aggregates written through their own services
 (WalletService, FundsService); each already exposes its own list. What none of them
 can answer is "what happened, in order", because interleaving four lists client-side
 needs a timestamp every one of them must agree on. This service is that join, done
 once in the hub over the Postgres projections.

 Read-only: it moves no money and owns no state. Every RPC acts on the caller's own
 access-token `sub`. Amounts are decimal USDT STRINGS (proto3 has no u128; a string is
 lossless and matches proto-loader's `longs: String`).
 See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and piggybank/core/PATTERNS.md.

tags.name: banking.v1.UsersService
tags.description:
UsersService — investor accounts and their investments.

 Identity metadata is the Postgres control plane; money is read live from the
 authoritative TigerBeetle ledger and is NEVER re-bookkept in Postgres. Every
 RPC is authorized from the verified access-token Claims injected by core's
 inbound auth layer; self-service RPCs act on the caller's own `sub`, admin RPCs
 are gated by the hub's admin allowlist (config). See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

tags.name: concierge.v1.UserDirectory
tags.description:
UserDirectory — the authoritative user/identity control plane.

 Owns investor accounts and their profile metadata. This is the identity plane:
 money lives in the separate banking plane and is NEVER mirrored here. Every RPC
 is authorized from the verified access-token Claims injected by the inbound auth
 layer; self-service RPCs act on the caller's own `sub`, admin RPCs are gated by
 the admin allowlist (config).

tags.name: concierge.v1.AuthService
tags.description:
AuthService — the concierge plane's token issuance and authorization surface.

 Issues first-party asymmetric JWTs (EdDSA/Ed25519) after Google OAuth2 sign-in,
 rotates refresh tokens, and publishes verification keys. Services do NOT call
 this per request to authorize: they verify access tokens locally against the
 cached JWKS via the shared `evconcierge_auth` flow (no round trip, no
 per-service token storage). They DO call `Jwks` periodically to refresh that
 cache, since concierge speaks only gRPC (no HTTP `.well-known` endpoint).

 The cabinet BFF is the OAuth confidential client. It runs the browser-facing
 authorize redirect (PKCE + state + nonce) and then calls `Exchange`
 server-to-server with the Google authorization code; the auth module performs
 the confidential code→token exchange with Google, validates Google's id_token,
 and discards it — Google's token is never forwarded inward.

tags.name: concierge.v1.GovernanceService
tags.description:
GovernanceService — the fund's OWNERSHIP plane: who holds `Role::Owner`, and the
 consilium that must agree before a seat is taken away.

 WHY OWNERSHIP LIVES HERE. A seat is `users.role`, a concierge-owned fact, and the
 bridge to the money plane is one-way. Only this plane may mutate it, so only this
 plane can authorize the mutation. The money plane runs its own, separate consilium
 over its own mirrored roster — neither plane trusts the other's verdict.

 THE RULE. A removal passes when EITHER
   (a) the target accepts it from their own mailbox, OR
   (b) every owner except the target and the initiator votes to remove.

 Path (b) is unanimity over `owners \ {target, initiator}`. With exactly two owners
 that set is EMPTY and unanimity over it is vacuously true — which would let either
 owner expel the other unilaterally. Path (b) therefore requires at least ONE eligible
 peer voter; with two owners only path (a) exists.

 FLOOR. A removal may not leave fewer than TWO owners. Two suspends payouts — the
 money plane's `floor(N/2)+1` threshold is unreachable below three — but that is
 recoverable, because two owners can still admit a third. A floor of three was the
 earlier draft and it was wrong: at exactly three owners it made a bad actor
 unremovable forever, and a permanent deadlock is worse than a recoverable pause.

 ADMISSION IS GOVERNED TOO, and it is the reason the rest of this holds. Granting a
 seat is its own consilium: unanimity of `owners \ {initiator}`, with at least one such
 peer. Without it a bad actor mints sock puppets BEFORE opening an invoice and then
 reaches quorum legitimately — 2 honest owners plus 4 puppets is N=7, threshold 4,
 voters 6 — and snapshotting the roster cannot help, because the stuffing already
 happened. Unanimity rather than a majority, because a minority must never be able to
 grow itself into a majority.

 See banking's docs/CONSILIUM.md for the whole policy.

tags.name: concierge.v1.OwnerRemovalApprovalService
tags.description:
OwnerRemovalApprovalService — the surface the TARGET of a removal reaches from their
 mailbox. Mounted outside the user-auth layer, like AuthService: the emailed token is
 the credential, and the person clicking may not be signed in.

 The read is side-effect free because mail scanners issue automatic requests for every
 URL in a message; accepting requires the secret code from the same mail.

tags.name: concierge.v1.MailRelayService
tags.description:
MailRelayService — the one seam over which the MONEY plane asks this plane to send a
 governance mail, because this plane owns the only mailer (lettre + the delivery queue
 + backoff + the daily budget) and standing up a second one would duplicate all of it.

 Authenticated by the shared banking↔concierge service secret, compared in constant
 time, and mounted outside the user-auth layer exactly as the lifecycle bridge is.

 The payload is TYPED, never rendered HTML: this plane renders it. A compromised money
 plane must not be able to put arbitrary markup into an owner's mailbox.

 This path deliberately bypasses notification preferences. `NotificationService.Emit`
 is opt-out on both channels, and a security mail that a subscriber can silently
 switch off is not a security mail.
